question: The United States topped the medal table at St Louis in 1904. Roughly what share of all competitors were American?
answer: About four in five. Few Europeans made the long, costly trip to Missouri, so most events were contests among Americans, and several were national championships in all but name. The host's huge medal haul measured the entry list more than the athletes. A table ranks only those who turned up.
move: Before praising a winner, ask who else was able to enter.
ask: When I praise a winner, do I know who else was actually able to enter?
trap: Assuming an Olympic field was international, as today's fields are.
reference: Mallon, The 1904 Olympic Games: Results for All Competitors in All Events, McFarland, 1999
